biomarkers.name: MYB / MYBL1 rearrangement including MYB-NFIB fusion (in adenoid cystic subtype)
biomarkers.prevalence: MYB activation/rearrangement in a majority of adenoid cystic carcinomas; MYB-NFIB fusion in a substantial subset (commonly reported around 40-60%)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports diagnosis of adenoid cystic carcinoma; biology parallels salivary ACC

biomarkers.name: PD-L1, TP53 (in tracheal SCC subtype)
biomarkers.prevalence: Not well defined specifically for primary tracheal SCC; TP53 alterations and variable PD-L1 expression have been reported, but site-specific prevalence is not established as for lung / head and neck SCC
biomarkers.clinical_use: If needed clinically, biomarker workup generally follows principles used for anatomically and histologically similar SCCs, recognizing limited trachea-specific evidence

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Two dominant subtypes: squamous cell carcinoma and adenoid cystic carcinoma; together they account for most primary tracheal carcinomas
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Follows relevant subtype grading (SCC or ACC)

tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: SCC: desmoplastic. ACC: characteristic reduplicated basement membrane material

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Squamous cell carcinoma from tracheal surface epithelium/basal cells; adenoid cystic carcinoma from tracheal submucosal glands (analogous to salivary ACC)
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Endoderm — foregut (trachea forms from laryngotracheal tube)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: SCC: keratinizing squamous; ACC: biphasic luminal + myoepithelial
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Tracheal ACC shares core MYB-pathway biology with salivary ACC and can be regarded as the same trans-anatomic lineage-defined disease
